classification.difficultyReason: Combine exact related angles with quadrant reasoning and draw a diagram for every equation.

content.prompt: Without using your calculator, find the angles $\theta$, between $0^\circ$ and $360^\circ$ inclusive, for which (draw a diagram in each case):

answer.worked:
Sine is positive in quadrants I and II. The related angle is $30^\circ$ because $\sin30^\circ=\frac12$.

$$\begin{align*}\theta&=30^\circ\text{ or }180^\circ-30^\circ\\\theta&=30^\circ\text{ or }150^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Authored unit-circle solution with rays in quadrants I and II.

answer.worked:
Tangent is positive in quadrants I and III. The related angle is $60^\circ$ because $\tan60^\circ=\sqrt3$.

$$\begin{align*}\theta&=60^\circ\text{ or }180^\circ+60^\circ\\\theta&=60^\circ\text{ or }240^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Authored unit-circle solution with rays in quadrants I and III.
spec.mathematics: Angles 60 and 240 degrees have tangent sqrt(3).

answer.worked:
Cosine is positive in quadrants I and IV. The related angle is $45^\circ$ because $\cos45^\circ=\frac1{\sqrt2}$.

$$\begin{align*}\theta&=45^\circ\text{ or }360^\circ-45^\circ\\\theta&=45^\circ\text{ or }315^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Authored unit-circle solution with rays in quadrants I and IV.

answer.worked:
Cosine is negative in quadrants II and III. The related angle is $60^\circ$ because $\cos60^\circ=\frac12$.

$$\begin{align*}\theta&=180^\circ-60^\circ\text{ or }180^\circ+60^\circ\\\theta&=120^\circ\text{ or }240^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Authored unit-circle solution with rays in quadrants II and III.

answer.worked:
Sine is negative in quadrants III and IV. The related angle is $60^\circ$ because $\sin60^\circ=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}$.

$$\begin{align*}\theta&=180^\circ+60^\circ\text{ or }360^\circ-60^\circ\\\theta&=240^\circ\text{ or }300^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Authored unit-circle solution with rays in quadrants III and IV.

answer.worked:
Tangent is positive in quadrants I and III. The related angle is $45^\circ$ because $\tan45^\circ=1$.

$$\begin{align*}\theta&=45^\circ\text{ or }180^\circ+45^\circ\\\theta&=45^\circ\text{ or }225^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Authored unit-circle solution with rays in quadrants I and III.
